 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. When Chicago Blackhawks captain Connor Bedard had to miss the first six games of the season after his shoulder surgery recovery, many wondered how he would look when he returned to the lineup.
 Now, 14 games in for him, he hasn't missed a beat.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In fact, he looks like he is only getting better.
 How Bedard continues to step up
 The stats can tell you Bedard's story from afar. He is the Blackhawks leading scorer with 17 points and leads in assists with 11. There is another stat that is interesting: he currently has 12 hits, and his career-high came in his rookie season (54). Now, he is on pace for 72 hits.
 Another stat that stands out is that Bedard is currently on pace for 102 points, which would exceed his career-high of 75 points last season. He is also on a three-game point streak (4 points).
 Bedard has been playing on the top line with Roman Kantserov, and those two have developed solid chemistry. His individual play stands out, too, with his creativity in driving offense while also using his body to defend , including blocking shots.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Then, there is Bedard's presence on the power play, which is starting to find its stride after a bumpy start, as the power play has three goals in the last two games.
 Bedard leads the team in power-play points (6).
 He is producing in every way the Blackhawks need and expect him to. But the way he keeps elevating his game over time comes as no surprise. Especially to his teammates.
 Ryan Donato shared with me at practice what he has seen from Bedard: "I mean, he's just a special player, right? He's a guy that is relentless in his effort and preparing and bringing it every night. And he's a guy we obviously look up to and heavily rely on. So he's doing his job, and I think he always wants to get better and continue to grow, and that's what separates him from the rest. And he's fun to be a teammate with, and it's awesome to be along with. Hopefully, he can continue to do that for us."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Great players are expected to produce, but another part of that is consistency. 
 Head coach Jeff Blashill said at practice, "I think Connor's been pretty consistent in his game throughout the season, to be real honest with you. I mean, maybe there's a game or two where I didn't think he quite had his best stuff. But overall, I think he's been pretty consistent. He's created on a pretty consistent basis. I think there's still even more production, even though he's producing at a pretty good rate. I think if probably the power play could heat up even more, that he had a lot of production there, but I think he's played at a high, high level. I think he's become a really good two-way centerman, and two-way means winning, and he's been a good model that way."
 Overall, the Blackhawks are not where they want to be in the standings, as they sit second-worst in the NHL. But the organization maintains belief in the team they have in the long run.
 Bedard continues to be a huge part of that of that why.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement How he has started this season, despite missing some time, the effect he has had on his teammates, and how his production is translating on the ice has been a bright spot.
